MATERIAL REQUIREMENTS PLANNING | E5 SYSTEM TESTING
Page 1
Black Box System Testing of the Material Planning 
System
Experiment 5 | English technical report | 22 October 2026
This report evaluates the implemented material planning system against its user requirements through 
external HTTP requests and real browser operations. The final HTTP run completed 125 cases, with 
125 passing. Browser suites supplied 65 additional passing checks. A CSV field-length defect found by 
boundary testing was corrected and retested. An intermittent Windows connection reset on an 
oversized request remains a documented transport observation.

1 Objectives and requirements
The E5 guide requires at least as many important modules or subsystems as group members, explicit 
preconditions and postconditions, test cases combining equivalence partitioning and boundary value 
analysis, and an English report. The three selected functional groups cover the six existing subsystems 
and exceed the two-member minimum. Grouping S2 to S5 into one external calculation scenario does 
not redefine the E2 architecture.
Expected results come from the written BR01 to BR09 rules, FR01 to FR08 acceptance conditions, 
CSV limits and persistence behavior. Internal coverage, private functions and database tables are not 
used to decide pass or fail. Source files were inspected only to identify public interfaces and diagnose 
observed defects; the black-box runner imports no application modules.

Invalid inputs intentionally violate these preconditions one at a time where practical. Their expected 
postcondition is an informative rejection with no partial persistence. Cross-record consistency cases 
cover relationships that individual field partitions cannot express.
2.1 Acceptance limits
Task demand and BOM usage are positive integers; stock and lead time are nonnegative integers; 
priority is 1, 2 or 3. Reserved stock must not exceed on-hand stock. CSV numeric inputs and the 
browser editor are restricted to the JavaScript safe-integer maximum 9007199254740991. The native 
JSON calculation interface uses Python integers and does not impose that same upper bound. These are 
separate entry-point contracts.
Each CSV file is limited to 500000 UTF-8 bytes and 5000 records. The combined HTTP JSON request 
is limited to 2000000 bytes. Boundary tests keep other constraints valid: the row-limit fixture stays 
below the byte limit, while the file-size fixture has only two material rows and uses one long name 
field.

All 371 recorded HTTP exchanges have request/response artifacts, except a transport exception would

Table 3.1 Base fixture
Record Fields
Material P MAKE product; unit pcs; lead time 2 days
Material R BUY raw material; unit pcs; lead time 3 days; minimum 0; purchase multiple 5
BOM P requires 2 units of R
Stocks P and R each have on_hand 0 and reserved 0; snapshot date 2026-11-01
Task T1 Product P; quantity 10; due 2026-11-20; priority 2; selected
Request Baseline 2026-11-01; rule version prototype-v0.2; request ID E5
Independent base oracle: P has no stock, so manufacture 10. Start P on 18 November. Raw demand is 
10 times 2, or 20. No raw stock exists; 20 already meets the multiple of 5, so purchase 20 for arrival on 
18 November and order on 15 November. No date precedes the baseline.
The BUY-root variant removes P and all BOM edges, keeps R and its stock, and points T1 directly to 
R. The multilevel fixture adds S: P requires 2 S and S requires 3 R. With P stock 2, S stock 4 and R 
on_hand 5/reserved 1, demand10 gives P8, S12, raw gross36, raw gap32 and purchase35. S lead time1 
makes the raw arrival17 November and order14 November.

6 Executed HTTP case register
Each row reports a specific executed case. Base fixture fields remain unchanged unless the scenario 
states otherwise. The evidence files contain exact inputs and complete outputs. VALID cases 
additionally require HTTP200 and a saved batch. INVALID planning cases additionally require 
HTTP200, at least one located error, unchanged history, and no saved_batch field. CSV cases 
additionally require HTTP200 and unchanged saved workspace and history. These repeated checks are 
abbreviated in the tables.
Output notation uses JSON arrays. Purchase rows are [material, arrival date, quantity, order date]; 
make rows are [material, quantity, start date]. Empty arrays mean no rows. Boolean true means the

9 Result interpretation and limitations
The selected cases support the stated quantity, stock, BOM, date, import, persistence and export 
requirements. Expected values are concrete outputs derived before execution from the business rules. 
Where full snapshots are compared, a mismatch is visible even if headline quantities are unchanged. 
Invalid input tests also verify that rejection does not create a history batch.
Passing these cases does not prove correctness for every graph or all inputs. This phase does not 
exhaust concurrent HTTP clients, disk-full failures, every CSV encoding, every graph depth, 
alternative browsers or operating systems. Version-conflict behavior is tested with stale revisions and 
two browser pages, not a high-load concurrency benchmark. The all-member academic review and 
personal contribution statements remain pending.
